title: Add graceful shutdown with in‑flight request draining
description: Provides a production‑ready shutdown flow that stops accepting new connections, waits for active requests to finish, and forces termination after a timeout. This prevents dropped requests during deployments or restarts and ensures resources are cleaned up safely.
testCases: When SIGTERM is received, the server stops accepting new connections within 100 ms.
Active requests are allowed to complete before the process exits, up to a configurable timeout (default 5 s).
If the timeout expires, remaining connections are force‑closed and the process exits with code 1.
acceptance: The framework exports a `closeGracefully(timeout?)` method; invoking it (or receiving SIGINT/SIGTERM) returns a promise that resolves after all in‑flight requests finish or the timeout elapses. No new requests are accepted after shutdown begins, and the process exits cleanly with appropriate exit codes.
reason: Deployments and container restarts are common in production; without graceful shutdown, in‑flight HTTP requests are abruptly terminated, leading to data loss and poor user experience. Adding this feature makes yantraverse suitable for high‑availability environments.
